362785.title: The induced-path conjecture for the graphs $G_{q,p}$
362785.statement: Let $q\geq 3$ be odd, let $p\geq 1$, and let $G_{q,p}$ be the graph constructed in the paper. Here, $P_t$ denotes the path on $t$ vertices, and a graph is **$P_t$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $P_t$. **Induced-path conjecture.** For every $p\geq 1$, the graph $G_{q,p}$ is $P_{3q-2}$-free. This would improve the general bound from Theorem~; the case $q=3$ is supported by the known $P_7$-freeness of $G_{3,p}$, while the conjecture remains open for the other cases discussed here.

362816.title: Derangement representation bound for finite graphs
362816.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. Write $drn(G)$ for its derangement representation number and $p(G)$ for its order, and let

$$
\mathcal{F}=\{\overline{K_2},\overline{K_3},P_3\}.
$$

**Derangement representation conjecture.** For every finite graph $G$ except the graphs in $\mathcal{F}$,

$$
drn(G)\leq p(G).
$$

The conjecture summarizes the examples reviewed in the paper, for which the derangement representation number is less than the order apart from the three listed exceptions. Its general validity for finite graphs remains open.

362880.title: Finite forbidden-subdiagram conjecture for shellable Kohnert posets
362880.statement: Let $D$ be a diagram, let $\mathcal{P}(D)$ be its Kohnert poset, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite collection of families of subdiagrams. **Finite forbidden-subdiagram conjecture.** There exists a finite number of families of subdiagrams $\mathcal{F}$ such that, for every diagram $D$, $\mathcal{P}(D)$ is shellable if and only if there is no $\widetilde{D}\in\mathcal{P}(D)$ containing a subdiagram from $\mathcal{F}$. This conjecture proposes a finite forbidden-subdiagram characterization of shellability, whereas the paper states that a complete general characterization was not obtained.

363028.title: The larger grid graph conjecture for Trail Trap
363028.statement: Let $P_m$ and $P_n$ be paths on $m$ and $n$ vertices, respectively, and let $P_m\square P_n$ be their Cartesian product, the $(m,n)$ grid graph. Let ${\rm P}{2}$ denote the second player in Trail Trap. A graph is ${\rm P}{2}$-win if the second player has a winning strategy. **Larger grid graph conjecture.** For any $m,n\geq 3$, the grid graph $P_m\square P_n$ is ${\rm P}{2}$-win. The paper proves several parity-based cases, but the full assertion for all $m,n\geq 3$ remains open.

363373.title: Linusson's bunkbed conjecture for hypergraph percolation
363373.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypergraph and let $T\subseteq V(\mathcal{H})$ be a set of posts. In the conditioned model $E_4^T(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}})$, precisely one of the two copies of each hyperedge is retained, and precisely the vertical edges at vertices in $T$ are retained. For vertices $u,v\in V(\mathcal{H})$, write $\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(u^{(0)}\xleftrightarrow{E_4^T(\mathcal{H})}v^{(i)})$ for bidirectional connectivity. **Linusson's hypergraph bunkbed conjecture.** For every hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ and every $T\subseteq V(\mathcal{H})$,

$$
\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(u^{(0)}\xleftrightarrow{E_4^T(\mathcal{H})}v^{(0)})\geq \operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(u^{(0)}\xleftrightarrow{E_4^T(\mathcal{H})}v^{(1)}).
$$

This conjecture is disproved in the paper by an explicit hypergraph example.

363445.title: The sparse paving characterization by Schubert coefficients
363445.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected matroid of rank $r$ on $[n]$. Write $U_{r,n}$ for the uniform matroid of rank $r$ on $[n]$, let $d_\lambda(M)$ denote the Schubert coefficient indexed by a partition $\lambda$, and let $h^c$ denote the complement of the hook partition $h$. **Sparse paving characterization.** $M$ is sparse paving if and only if

$$
d_\lambda(M)=d_\lambda(U_{r,n})
$$

for all partitions $\lambda\neq h^c$. The paper proves the forward implication for connected sparse paving matroids; the converse remains conjectural.

363809.title: The upper-bound conjecture for the alphabet size of anagram-free words
363809.statement:
Fix $k\geqslant 1$. A word is called **$k$-anagram-free** if every factor $F$ satisfies $\alpha(F)\geqslant k+1$, where $\alpha(F)$ is the least number of cuts needed to decompose $F$ into factors that can be rearranged into a pair of anagrams. Let $a(k)$ be the least alphabet size for which arbitrarily long $k$-anagram-free words exist. **Upper-bound conjecture for $a(k)$.** For every $k\geqslant 1$,

$$
a(k)\leqslant k+3.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed bound in its closing remarks. The only stated value is $a(1)=4$, and the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.

363910.title: The FKM conjecture on pairwise partition regularity of quadratic equations
363910.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in \mathbb{Z}$ be nonzero, and consider the homogeneous quadratic equation

$$
a x^2+b y^2=c z^2.
$$

An equation is **partition regular with respect to $x,y$** if every finite coloring of the positive integers admits a monochromatic choice of $x,y$ for which the equation has a solution in the remaining variable $z$.

**FKM's pairwise partition-regularity conjecture.** If at least one of $ac$, $bc$, or $(a+b)c$ is a square, then $a x^2+b y^2=c z^2$ is partition regular with respect to $x,y$.

The assumptions are motivated by necessary conditions developed in the paper, and the conjecture is known when $ac$ or $bc$ is a square. The remaining cases, including the equation $x^2+y^2=2z^2$ with respect to any two variables, remain open.

363938.title: The relaxed confusion-number bound conjecture for signed graphs
363938.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n \geq 1$, let $\sigma$ be a signing of $G$, and let $\ell(G,\sigma)$ denote the frustration index. Let $C_r(G,\sigma)$ denote the relaxed confusion number. **The relaxed confusion-number bound conjecture.** For every signed graph $(G,\sigma)$,

$$
C_r(G,\sigma) \leq \min\left\{\ell(G,\sigma),\left\lceil \frac{3n}{5}-4 \right\rceil\right\}.
$$

This conjecture combines the proposed general confusion-number bound with the expectation that the relaxed confusion number is at most the frustration index. The paper gives supporting results for particular signed graphs but leaves the general assertion open.

363994.title: Subcube extremality for the Hamming cube's beta-isoperimetric profile
363994.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}_\beta$ be the $\beta$-isoperimetric profile of the Hamming cube, defined for dyadic rationals $x\in\mathcal{Q}$ by

$$
\mathcal{B}_\beta(x)=\inf_{n\ge 1}\inf_{\substack{A\subset\{0,1\}^n\\|A|=x}}\mathbf{E}h_A^\beta.
$$

Here $h_A$ denotes the relevant Hamming-cube boundary function, and $k\ge 1$ is an integer.

**Subcube extremality conjecture.** For all $\beta\ge\frac12$ and all $k\ge 1$,

$$
\mathcal{B}_\beta(2^{-k})=2^{-k}k^\beta.
$$

The equality is attained by codimension-$k$ subcubes. Subcubes are known to be extremizers when $\beta=1$, while their extremality for $\beta<1$ is not otherwise known.

364116.title: The Prim'–Cayley fixed-point sum conjecture
364116.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Prim}'$ and $\operatorname{Cay}$ be the species of primitive objects and Cayley permutations, respectively. For a Cayley permutation $w=w_1\cdots w_n$, let

$$
\textsc{fix}(w)=\{i:w_i=i\}
$$

be its set of fixed points. **The Prim'–Cayley fixed-point sum conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$,

$$
\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{Prim}'[n]|=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{w\in\operatorname{Cay}[n]}\sum_{i=1}^n w_i=\sum_{w\in\operatorname{Cay}[n]}\sum_{i\in\textsc{fix}(w)}i.
$$

The conjecture concerns a further relationship between the species $\operatorname{Prim}'$ and $\operatorname{Cay}$ beyond the known species equality $\operatorname{Prim}'=\operatorname{Cay}^2$. The paper reports that no bijective proof of that equality was found; no resolution of this fixed-point sum conjecture is given.

364120.title: The total equality conditions for all loopless matroids
364120.statement: Let $\mathscr{M}$ be a loopless matroid of rank $r\geq 2$ with ground set $X$, and let $R\subseteq X$. Suppose that $\textrm{p}(\mathscr{M},R,0)>0$ and $\textrm{p}(\mathscr{M},R,r)>0$. The total equality conditions in Theorem~ assert equivalent conditions involving equality in the Stanley--Yan inequalities and the existence of a constant $s>0$ such that $|\operatorname{Par}_{\mathscr{M}}(x)\cap R|=s|\operatorname{Par}_{\mathscr{M}}(x)\cap(X-R)|$ for every $x\in X$. **Total equality conjecture.** The conclusion of Theorem~ holds for all loopless matroids. The theorem is stated for loopless regular matroids; the conjecture asks whether regularity can be removed.

364351.title: Bayer et al.'s shellability conjecture for cut complexes of grid graphs
364351.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{m\times n}$ denote the $m\times n$ grid graph, and let $\Delta_k(G)$ be the $k$-cut complex of a graph $G$. A simplicial complex is **shellable** if its facets admit a shelling order. **Bayer et al.'s shellability conjecture.** The complex $\Delta_k(\mathcal{G}_{m\times n})$ is shellable for all

$$
3\leq k\leq mn-3.
$$

This concerns the shellability of cut complexes across the full stated range of $k$. The source says that Bayer et al. had already proved shellability for $k=3$, while the displayed assertion is presented as their conjecture; no resolution of the full range is given here.

364355.title: The matrix-set filling conjecture
364355.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Mat}^{n\times n}_q$ denote the additive group of $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb F_q$, and let $\operatorname{GL}(n,q)$ act by left and right multiplication. **Matrix-set filling conjecture.** For every $c>0$ there is an integer $\mu=\mu(c)$ such that, whenever $X_1,\ldots,X_\mu\subseteq\operatorname{Mat}^{n\times n}_q$ satisfy $|X_i|\ge q^{cn^2}$, there are $a_i,b_i\in\operatorname{GL}(n,q)$ such that

$$
a_1X_1b_1+\cdots+a_\mu X_\mu b_\mu=\operatorname{Mat}^{n\times n}_q.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem proved in the paper, but the excerpt gives no resolution status.

364471.title: Griggs's chain decomposition conjecture for the Boolean algebra
364471.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the Boolean algebra of all subsets of $[n]$, ordered by inclusion. A chain decomposition of $B_n$ has a type, namely the partition obtained by rearranging its chain sizes in weakly decreasing order. For partitions $\lambda$ and $
u$ of $2^n$, write $\lambda\unlhd
u$ when $\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\leq\sum_{i=1}^k
u_i$ for every $k\geq1$. **Griggs's conjecture.** If a partition $\lambda$ of $2^n$ satisfies $\lambda\unlhd
u$, where $
u$ is the partition corresponding to the symmetric chain decomposition of $B_n$, then $B_n$ has a chain decomposition of type $\lambda$. This conjecture is equivalent to the assertion that the incomparability graph of $B_n$ is nice; the paper presents it as motivation for studying Schur positivity.

364559.title: A coefficient pattern conjecture for the characteristic polynomial of the substitution matrix
364559.statement:
Let $n$ be odd with $n\geq 5$, let $M_n$ be the substitution matrix, and write its characteristic polynomial as

$$
p_n(x)=-(x-1)q_n(x).
$$

The coefficients of $q_n(x)$ in standard form are arranged according to the pattern described in the paper: their signs from left to right are $+,-,-,+,+,-,-,+,+,\ldots$, the last two coefficients in each row are $1$ or $-1$ depending on $n$, and each remaining coefficient is obtained by summing the absolute values of the two numbers indicated by adjacent segments of the same color and assigning the sign determined by its position. **Coefficient-pattern conjecture.** This coefficient pattern holds for all odd $n\geq 5$.

364626.title: Finiteness conjecture for connected graphs with odd metamour period
364626.statement:
A graph's **metamour period** is the least positive integer $k$ for which its iterated metamour graph returns to the original graph, under the metamour operation used in the paper. Let $k$ range over the positive odd integers.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For each odd $k\in \mathbb{Z}^+$, there exist only finitely many connected graphs with metamour period $k$.

The paper has already classified the connected graphs with metamour period $3$: they are $C_7$ and $C_9$. The conjecture predicts analogous finiteness for every odd period, and the classification of such graphs remains open in general.

364642.title: Saikia–Sarma–Sellers conjecture for overpartition tuples with even length
364642.statement:
Let $i\geq 1$, let $n\geq 0$, and let $r$ be odd. The function $\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(n)$ counts overpartition $2^i r$-tuples with odd parts. **Saikia–Sarma–Sellers' conjecture.** For all such $i,n,r$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+1)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{i+1}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+2)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{2i+1}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+3)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{i+3}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+4)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{2i+4}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+5)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{i+2}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+6)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{2i+3}},\\
\overline{OPT}_{2^i r}(8n+7)&\equiv0\pmod{2^{i+4}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These congruences generalize the preceding divisibility theorem for even $k$; the source attributes them to Saikia, Sarma, and Sellers and presents them as conjectural.

364883.title: Regularity propagation conjecture for disjoint Golomb rulers
364883.statement:
For positive integers $I$ and $J$, let $H(I,J)$ denote the least $n$ admitting $I$ disjoint $J$-mark Golomb rulers in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A DGR is **regular** when $n=IJ$. **Regularity propagation conjecture.** If

$$
H(I_0,J)=I_0J,
$$

then

$$
H(I,J)=IJ
$$

for every integer $I>I_0$. The conjecture predicts that regularity at one value of the number of rulers propagates to all larger values; it is used in the paper as a proposed structural principle and remains unproved.

364884.title: Extension conjecture for regular disjoint Golomb rulers
364884.statement: Let $I$ and $J$ be positive integers. A regular $(I+1,J,(I+1)J)$-DGR is a collection of $I+1$ disjoint $J$-mark Golomb rulers partitioning $\{1,\ldots,(I+1)J\}$. **Regular extension conjecture.** For every Golomb ruler $A_1\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,(I+1)J\}$ with $|A_1|=J$, if $H(I,J)=IJ$, then there exists a regular $(I+1,J,(I+1)J)$-DGR containing $A_1$. This strengthens the preceding regularity idea by requiring extension of every prescribed ruler; it is stated as a conjecture without a proof.
